title: My Bedtime Checklist
text:
Every night I follow my bedtime checklist. Mom wrote it in {color} marker and taped it to my door.

First, I take a warm bath with my rubber duck and {number} {plural noun}. Then I put on my pajamas with little {plural noun} all over them. They are very {adjective}.

Next, I brush my teeth for two whole minutes. Dad says to brush {adverb}, the way a {animal} would. Then I pick one book. My favorite is about a {noun} who learns how to {verb}.

Last, I get a sip of water. Everybody in the house gives me a {adjective} hug, even the cat, who {past tense verb}. I turn on my night light, which is shaped like a {noun}. Then I close my eyes and dream about {verb ending in ing}.

title: My Dream Report for Tuesday Night
text:
Dream report by Leo, age six. I went to sleep at eight o'clock and woke up at seven. Here is what I dreamed.

I was the captain of a big boat made of {plural noun}. My first mate was a {adjective} {animal} named Mr. Wiggles. We sailed {adverb} across a sea of warm {food}. Every time a wave came, Mr. Wiggles shouted "{exclamation}!" and did a little dance.

Then we landed on an island where everybody was {verb ending in ing}. The trees grew {plural noun} instead of coconuts. The mayor gave me a golden {noun} and asked me to {verb} at the island party. Everybody cheered {adverb}.

Right before I woke up, my dog jumped on my bed, and the whole island {past tense verb}. I told Mom about it at breakfast. She said it sounded like a {adjective} dream.

title: How to Sing a Lullaby to a Baby Brother
text:
My baby brother Max does not like to go to sleep. Mom taught me how to sing him a lullaby, and now I am an expert.

First, make the room dark and quiet. Turn on his night light, which is shaped like a {noun}. Give Max his favorite {noun} to hold. He likes to chew on it until it is {adjective}.

Next, sit in the rocking chair and rock {adverb}. Sing very softly: "Hush little baby, don't you {verb}, Mama's going to buy you {number} {plural noun}." If his eyes are still open, wiggle your {body part} and sing about a sleepy {animal} who is {verb ending in ing} on a cloud.

When Max closes his eyes, tiptoe out of the room. Do not {verb}, do not sneeze, and do not step on the {adjective} floorboard by the door. If he wakes up, start over and sing about {plural noun}.

title: Bedtime Roll Call for My Stuffed Animals
text:
Before I go to sleep, I take roll call so all my stuffed animals are in bed with me. I have {number} stuffed friends, so it takes a while.

First is Bear. Bear sleeps on my pillow because he is the most {adjective}. He is also very good at {verb ending in ing}. Next is Bunny, who always wants to {verb} before she falls asleep. Then comes Duck, who smells a little bit like {plural noun}. Tonight he is wearing a tiny {noun} on his head.

The newest one is a stuffed {animal} from Grandma. Her name is Princess {silly word}. She is a little shy, so I tuck her in {adverb} and tell her that we {past tense verb} at recess today.

Then I give everyone a {adjective} goodnight squeeze. Last night Mom found three {plural noun} and a sock under my blanket. She said they could stay, as long as they do not {verb} all night.

title: A Letter to the Moon
text:
Dear Moon, I can see you from my bedroom window every night. You are round and {adjective}, and you look like a big {noun} in the sky.

I have some questions for you. Do you ever get {adjective} from staying up all night? Do you have a pet {noun}? Do the stars help you {verb} when you are bored? My teacher says you are made of rock, but my brother says you are made of {food}. Please tell me who is right.

Tonight I am leaving a gift on my windowsill for you. It is a drawing of {number} {plural noun} having a picnic. I colored it {adverb} with my {adjective} crayons.

Mom says it is time to put away my {plural noun} and turn off the light. If you see me {verb ending in ing} in my sleep, please wave back with your {body part}. Love, Ruby

title: Tonight's Pillow Fort Forecast
text:

title: Rules for Reading a Bedtime Story
text:
In our house, Dad reads the bedtime story. After many years of practice, he has made some rules.

Rule one: The reader must use a different voice for every character. The dragon gets a deep voice, and the {noun} sounds like a {adjective} teapot. Rule two: The listener may ask {number} questions and no more. Last night my sister asked why the giant was afraid of {plural noun}. Dad {past tense verb} and said it was a good question.

Rule three: Nobody may {verb} during the sad part. Rule four: If the reader falls asleep first, the listener must tap him {adverb} on the {body part} and say, "Wake up, please." Rule five: Every story must end with somebody {verb ending in ing} happily ever after. Rule six: No snacks in bed, except one {food}.

If we follow the rules, Dad will read the one about the {adjective} pirate who found a treasure chest full of {plural noun}.

title: Grandpa's Sleepover Schedule
text:
I am sleeping over at Grandpa Walt's house tonight. Grandpa made a schedule and stuck it on the fridge with a magnet shaped like a {noun}.

At six o'clock, we eat dinner. Grandpa is making his famous spaghetti with {plural noun} on top and a side of {food}. At seven o'clock, we go outside to look at the stars and {verb} in the backyard. Grandpa says the brightest star is called {silly word}.

At eight o'clock, we put on pajamas and have warm milk. Grandpa stirs his milk {adverb} with a {adjective} spoon. Then he tells me about when he was a boy and {past tense verb} to school every day with his pet {noun}.

At nine o'clock, it is lights out. Grandpa checks the windows, gives me a {adjective} goodnight hug, and turns on his radio. He says he can only fall asleep while listening to {verb ending in ing} {plural noun}.

title: Reasons I Need Five More Minutes
text:
Dear Mom and Dad, I know it is bedtime. Here are some very good reasons why I need five more minutes.

Reason three: Tomorrow is Crazy Hat Day, and I still need to glue a {noun} on my hat. Reason four: The cat just {past tense verb} in the hallway, and I want to make sure she is okay. Reason five: I am a little bit hungry for {food}.

Reason six: I am wide awake and ready to {verb}. Look how {adverb} I can hop on one foot! Reason seven: My stuffed {animal} wants one more book about {verb ending in ing}.

If you say yes, I will go straight to sleep and dream about {plural noun}. Love, your {adjective} kid, Sam
